Abstract.AbstractText: Key findings Data from the National Vital Statistics System ● Infant mortality rates decreased as urbanization level increased, from 6.55 deaths per 1,000 births in rural counties to 6.20 in small and medium urban counties and 5.44 in large urban counties. ● Neonatal mortality rates were higher in rural counties than in large urban counties, and postneonatal mortality rates decreased as urbanization level increased. ● Mortality rates decreased as urbanization level increased for infants of mothers aged 20-29, 30-39, and 40 and over. ● For infants of non-Hispanic white and non-Hispanic black mothers, mortality rates were lowest in large urban counties.

Article.ArticleTitle: Infant Mortality Rates in Rural and Urban Areas in the United States, 2014.
